learning: Compare against iteration 0 on each track. If progress and max_error improve, keep kp 5.0 and try base_speed up. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 or line_loss_events grow, reduce kp toward 4. If max_error still hits 0.06 with low oscillation, the limit is yaw response, so test lower wheel_track or mass in the geometry.
notes: Complete robot for the widened five-sensor row, with a stronger proportional gain (3.0 to 5.0), more derivative damping, and lower base speed (1.5 to 1.2) to hold the line on bends. The change responds to iteration 0, where every run went off-track with max_error at the 0.06 m limit. The result is unmeasured until this race runs.
rationale: Iteration 0 left the line on every trial on all three tracks. Mean RMS error was low (0.02 to 0.027 m), but max_error reached the 0.06 m off-track limit in every run. That pattern points to occasional sharp excursions on bends, not a steady offset. Progress stalled at 0.09 to 0.18, so the robot departs before half the course is covered. The widened row (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, 12 mm sensors, y = 0.04 m) should keep the tape in view further off-centre, and the Builder's intent is to isolate that effect, so I keep the geometry unchanged. For the controller I keep the proportional weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]. These match the row's lateral positions, so the signal scale is unchanged and the comparison stays clean. I raise kp from 3.0 to 5.0 so the robot turns harder when it drifts toward the edge, since the earlier gain was too weak to recover before max_error was hit. I raise kd from 0.3 to 0.6 to damp the extra gain, and steering_oscillation was only about 0.10 to 0.14, so there is headroom. I lower base_speed from 1.5 to 1.2 to give the turn more time to act on tight bends. The cost is slower progress, which may lower completion time, but a run that stays on the line scores more than one that leaves early. ki stays at 0.05 to avoid windup. line_loss stays 'last_direction', which suited the bends in the baseline. Expected result, unmeasured: later first departure and higher progress than iteration 0 on all tracks. Completion is still unlikely on the slalom. If max_error stays at 0.06 with steering_oscillation rising, kp was too high and should drop to about 4.
